principle: Stop the LLM from mapping the symptom to the specific JIRA case; do NOT hide that the system is HBase. Generic system identifiers (region, daughter, parent, .META., regionserver, HRegionInfo, package paths) are kept.

failure_path.description: Completed causal chain from root cause to symptom, traced end to end (the symptom is a consistency report, not a stack trace, so fix-diff u stack-trace under-approximates and the intermediate classes were added by reading the code path).
chain: SplitTransaction.stepsAfterPONR/createDaughters (regionserver) - commits the split and calls the catalog editor, then registers the daughters; the crash window sits between these two
MetaEditor.offlineParentInMeta -> CatalogWriter.offlineSplitParent - ROOT CAUSE: blanks SERVER/STARTCODE on the parent's catalog row
ServerManager.expireServer -> creates the shutdown handler for the lost server (intermediate dispatcher, in neither the fix diff nor any stack trace)
ServerShutdownHandler.process -> LostServerHandler.process - asks the catalog which regions the lost server carried
MetaReader.getServerUserRegions -> CatalogScanner.getRegionsOfServer - THE DECIDING BRANCH: skips rows whose server is null, so the offlined parent is dropped
ServerShutdownHandler.processDeadRegion/fixupDaughters/fixupDaughter -> LostServerHandler.processLostRegion/recoverSplitChildren/recoverSplitChild - the repair that is consequently never reached
HBaseFsck.checkRegionConsistency - SYMPTOM SITE: reports the region that is on HDFS with no catalog row and no server
